newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda says to synchronise model cycle with Ford.
newsitem.headline: Mazda says to synchronise model cycle with Ford.

text.p: Motor Corp president Henry Wallace said on Thursday that Mazda and Ford Motor Co had agreed to synchronise vehicle production cycles, but said not all Mazda models would be affected.

Wallace told reporters that Mazda had also agreed with Ford to share a number of car platforms, comprising engines and transmissions, over a number of years. He declined to specify details such as how many platforms would be shared, for which models, or when the sharing would take place.
Asked what percentage of Mazda cars would be affected by platform sharing, Wallace said it would be a substantial proportion. He did not elaborate further.
Asked how the platform sharing plan would affect Mazda's production, Wallace said the volume of production would go up.

Mazda, Japan's fifth-ranked carmaker, is one-third owned by Ford. Their long-standing ties intensified last year when Wallace, a Ford official seconded to Mazda, took over as Mazda's president, setting himself the task of steering the ailing firm back to prosperity.
The platform-sharing, which has long been anticipated, will enable the two firms to cut development costs and cut the cost of auto parts, analysts have said.
